submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad early head, measured on every token including the first: plain English prose is active-weak about one text in four (0.2-0.4 of max, usually on the first one to three tokens such as 'She', 'Many', 'After', 'He said'), and non-English Latin-script prose (Turkish, Spanish, Polish, Portuguese) is active on nearly every token at 0.35-0.55, highest on diacritic byte-fragment tokens. It is strongest (0.6-1.0 of max) on the line-start indentation token of a C/Java/PHP block-comment line ('     ' before '*') when the previous comment line also began with indentation + '*' (it attends back to that earlier '*'), strong (0.4-0.5) on the newline ending the second or later of several equally indented code or ' *' lines, and on 'using' after a byte-order mark at document start (0.72); the only class predicted inactive is a numbered English list item 'D. <plain English sentence>' of 7-15 tokens, and markdown '-' bullets, '>' quotes and '#' comment lines stay at or below 0.3.

rival_explanations: Any repeated line prefix: the head fires on the line starts and newlines of any list-like text whose lines share a prefix, so markdown '-' bullets, '>' quotes and '#' comment lines should be as strong as Javadoc ' *' lines (I measured them at 0.2-0.3 of max, against 0.8).

Block-comment continuation only: the head tracks C-style '*' comment continuation lines, so indented code with no '*' (repeated 'a = 1;' lines, list arguments, closing braces) should stay inactive rather than reach 0.4-0.5 on its newlines.
